name: Minimum Modular
description: You have been given n distinct integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n . You can remove at most k of them. Find the minimum modular m ( m > 0) , so that for every pair of the remaining integers ( a i , a j ) , the following unequality holds: .
input_specification: The first line contains two integers n and k ( 1  ≤ n ≤ 5000, 0 ≤ k ≤ 4 ), which we have mentioned above. The second line contains n distinct integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n (0 ≤ a i ≤ 10 6 ) .
output_specification: Print a single positive integer — the minimum m .
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 303C — Minimum Modular [242. Sieve, Prime Factorization and Divisors]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every composite integer $X$ has at least one prime factor $\le \sqrt{X}$. Precomputing the Smallest Prime Factor (SPF) for all numbers up to $M$ via a linear sieve allows any $X \le M$ to be completely prime-factorized in $O(\log X)$ steps.
